instruction: I'm teaching syllable counting. Can you color one-syllable words in purple and multi-syllable words (2 or more syllables) in orange?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires coloring words by syllable count: purple for 1 syllable, orange for 2+ syllables. Uses simple vowel-group heuristic for syllable estimation. Most words in list are 1-syllable (all, do, no, say, want, am, eat, now, she, was, are, four, on, so, well, at, get, our, soon, went, ate, good, out, that, what, be, have, please, there, white, black, he, they, who, brown, ran, this, will, but, like, ride, too, with, came, must, saw, yes, did, new). Multi-syllable words: pretty (2), into (2), under (2). Uses fuzzy color matching.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Evaluator only checks words that ARE colored, but does not verify that ALL words are colored. If user colors 0 words or leaves words uncolored, evaluator returns 1.0 (pass)

Missing coverage check: Instruction requires coloring ALL one-syllable words in purple and ALL multi-syllable words in orange, but evaluator does not count or verify that all words in the document have been colored
Logic flaw in docs.py:69: 'if word and run.font.color and run.font.color.rgb:' - this condition skips runs without colors, meaning uncolored words are silently ignored
The evaluator would incorrectly pass if the document is unmodified (all words black/uncolored) or partially colored
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add a completeness check: Count total words in the document and verify that all non-empty words have colors applied
Add tracking for uncolored words: If any word lacks a color or has default black color, the evaluator should fail
Consider adding a minimum colored word count threshold based on known document content (e.g., must color at least 40+ words)
Alternative fix: Iterate through all words first, then check that each has the correct color (purple for 1-syllable, orange for 2+), failing if any word is uncolored or incorrectly colored
